001.evidence: we with Saporetti, Faucounau, Nahm, Duhoux, Olivier and Valério (Valério 2016, 652). On RASH Atab 004 it writes the Hurrian ew- of e-we-ta-sa-li, the name Nahm compares with ỉwrtḏl (Valério 2016, 372; DULAT 129).

002.evidence: ne with Nahm, Facchetti et al. and Valério (Valério 2016, 652); É. Masson's readings imply b/p (1974, 42). It gives a-ne-ni and a-ne-ja-ni, the second the ảnnyn spelled a-na-an-ia-nu and a-na-ni-ya-nu at Ugarit (DULAT 79).

004.evidence: ta/da with every proposer (Valério 2016, 652) and the homomorph with Linear A *01 da (Davis 2026b, 398). On RASH Atab 004 it writes the d of Danāni, da-na-nu at Ugarit, and the t of ʾIlī-ṯtamri (DULAT 274, 65).

006.evidence: pa with every proposer and the homomorph with Linear A *03 pa (Valério 2016, 652; Davis 2026b, 398). On RASH Atab 004 it writes the b of ʾIšbaʿli, i-ši-pa-li, i-ši-ᵈU at Ugarit (DULAT 112).

008.evidence: na with Sittig, Saporetti, Faucounau, Nahm, Olivier, Steele and Valério (Valério 2016, 652); Davis's homomorph is Linear A *05 to (Davis 2026b, 398), and É. Masson read tˣ. It gives Danāni, ta-na-ni, the dnn spelled da-na-nu at Ugarit (DULAT 274).

009.evidence: li with É. Masson, Saporetti, Faucounau, Nahm and Valério, against Sittig's so (Valério 2016, 652). On RASH Atab 004 it writes the l of ʾIlī- in ʾIlī-maliki, ʾIlyāni and ʾIlī-ṯtamri (DULAT 55, 66, 65).

011.evidence: pe with Faucounau, Nahm, Duhoux and Valério (Valério 2016, 652). On RASH Atab 004 it stands in B.19 as a sign, not a divider (Egetmeyer, in Steele (ed.) 2013, 111), in sa-pe-ri, Nahm's spr 'scribe' (Valério 2016, 389).

019.evidence: u with Faucounau, Nahm and Valério (Valério 2016, 653). On RASH Atab 004 it opens u-mi-mo-ti, the ủmmt of 'bn ủmmt' (DULAT 68), and u-la-mo-ri.

021.evidence: ko with Sittig, Saporetti, Faucounau, Nahm and Valério (Valério 2016, 653); Duhoux corrects HoChyMin's 022 to 021 in B.13 and B.16 (Steele (ed.) 2013, 39 n. 54). It writes the first syllable of Kôṯar in ko-sa-ra-pi, ku-šar-a-bi in the Akkadian texts of Ugarit (Kinlaw 1967, 75).

023.evidence: ti with every proposer but Sittig and the homomorph with Linear A *37 ti (Valério 2016, 653; Davis 2026b, 398). On RASH Atab 004 it closes a-ti, ʾAdī, a-du-ú and ad-di-ya at Ugarit (DULAT 23), and u-mi-mo-ti (DULAT 68).

025.evidence: ka with every proposer, É. Masson's ḫ/ġa among them (Valério 2016, 653). On RASH Atab 004 it writes q, g, ġ and k: Maʿqabiyi (DULAT 516: mʿqby), ʾAġlā and ʾAġalʾabī, on the aġl- of ảġli, a-ḫa-la-e, and ảglby, a-ga-li-bi (DULAT 29, 25), which Valério sets aside as matches for their ending and their vowels (2016, 363, 371), and Kabili (DULAT 423: ka-bu-li).

027.evidence: si with É. Masson, Saporetti, Faucounau, Nahm and Valério (Valério 2016, 653). On RASH Atab 004 it opens si-ja in B.17, where Valério reads si?-ja? (2016, 388).

028.evidence: nu with É. Masson (1974, 39) and Faucounau's n∂ (1977, 227); Saporetti and Woudhuizen read ni (Valério 2016, 364; Woudhuizen 2016, 30), Valério lu, Nahm ru. It closes bi-nu, Semitic bin- 'son', which stands eleven times on RASH Atab 004, seven of them between two names, as Ugaritic lists set 'PN bn PN' (DULAT 65). With 100 read ni, nu keeps the two signs apart. Valério holds that ni and nu were forced on the sign to explain the word (2016, 364).

035.evidence: we, the value Valério prefers to wi₂ for the Hurrian Ewen(n)i, as a strictly experimental one (2016, 385–386), and the cell of Table 5.27 that sets 35 under we beside wi₂ (442). Faucounau read wi and Valério's grids give wi₂ (Valério 2016, 653, 390); Nahm read me, É. Masson la. On RASH Atab 004 it gives e-we₂-ni, the name whose ewen- the Akkadian texts of Ugarit spell e-we-en- (Kinlaw 1967, 51). The subscript keeps it apart from 001.

037b.evidence: zi with Valério, who reads 37b, grapheme 41/37b, where HoChyMin prints 37 in A.09 (2016, 442, 548–549). On RASH Atab 004 it gives zi-ja-ni-ji, Siyanniyi, the gentilic syny that follows a name in 'PN syny' (DULAT 763), as Nahm also came to read it (Valério 2016, 380 n. 1011). Valério marks the value experimental (2016, 380).

038.evidence: e with Faucounau, Nahm and Valério (Valério 2016, 654); É. Masson read u. On RASH Atab 004 it opens the Hurrian names in ew-, e-we-ta-sa-li and e-wi-ni.

040.evidence: yi/ji with É. Masson, Nahm and Valério (Valério 2016, 654). On RASH Atab 004 it closes the gentilics that follow a name in A.04, A.09 and B.12, as É. Masson saw (1974, 38): Maʿqabiyi, of Maʿqabu, a town of Ugarit's plain (DULAT 516; Astour 1995, 65), and Siyanniyi, of Siyannu (DULAT 763).

051.evidence: pi/bi with É. Masson, Faucounau, Nahm and Valério (Valério 2016, 654); Saporetti's tabulated sa stands against. On RASH Atab 004 it writes /b/ in bi-nu 'son', in the final ʾabī of Kôṯar-ʾabī, ku-šar-a-bi in the Akkadian texts of Ugarit (Kinlaw 1967, 75), and in ʾAġalʾabī (DULAT 25: a-ga-li-bi), and /p/ in ʿAmmurapi, a-mu-ra-pí (DULAT 162).

055.evidence: ma with Nahm, Facchetti et al. and Valério (Valério 2016, 654); É. Masson read ša. On RASH Atab 004 it gives ʾIlī-maliki, i-li-ma-li-ki, the ỉlmlk of Ugarit (DULAT 55), and malki 'king', ma-ki, after bi-nu in B.15 and B.18.

058.evidence: ši with Nahm and Faucounau's š∂ (Valério 2016, 386, 389; Faucounau 1977, 233); É. Masson read ya, and Valério emends the sign to 25 in A.03, allowing 102 there too (2016, 547–548), and keeps it as lu??/58 in B.19 (2016, 388). Read ši, the corpus text gives two names of Ugarit: ʾIšbaʿli, i-ši-pa-li, the ỉšbʿl spelled i-ši-ᵈU (DULAT 112), and Šapši-maliki, sa-ši-ma-li-ki with the p in coda unwritten, the špšmlk spelled ᵈUTU-LUGAL, among others in the colophon of RS 20.32 (DULAT 825). Valério objects that the sign cannot share the value of 027 si (2016, 389).

069.evidence: ja with Nahm, Facchetti et al. and Valério (Valério 2016, 655). On RASH Atab 004 it closes si-ja in B.17.

070.evidence: ki with Saporetti, Faucounau, Nahm, Olivier and Valério (Valério 2016, 655); É. Masson read mi. On RASH Atab 004 it closes ʾIlī-maliki (DULAT 55: ỉlmlk) and malki 'king'.

071.evidence: ja with Nahm and Valério (Valério 2016, 655, 376); É. Masson read ṯ. On RASH Atab 004 it gives ʾIlyāni, i-li-ja-ni, the ỉlyn spelled DINGIR-ia-nu (DULAT 66), and ta-ja-ni, tyn (DULAT 871).

073.evidence: mo with Nahm and Valério (Valério 2016, 655), read 73 in B.12 for HoChyMin's 72 with Duhoux and Valério (Steele (ed.) 2013, 39 n. 54; Valério 2016, 547 n. 1242). On RASH Atab 004 it writes the m of Môtu in u-mi-mo-ti (DULAT 68: ủmmt) and of Amurru in u-la-mo-ri.

074.evidence: mu with Faucounau, who read 102-074-082-051 a-mu-sa-pi and 102-074-075-051 a-mu-ra-bi (1980, 382), and mV with É. Masson (Valério 2016, 655); Valério reads wi and takes it for /b/ (2016, 382–385). Read mu, the B.17 group is ʿAmmurapi, spelled a-mu-ra-pí and am-mu-ra-pí at Ugarit, the name of its king (DULAT 162; Kinlaw 1967, 22). The value was chosen on this name, which therefore does not test it.

075.evidence: ra with É. Masson, Saporetti, Faucounau, Nahm and Valério (Valério 2016, 655). On RASH Atab 004 it writes the r of Kôṯar-ʾabī, ku-šar-a-bi (Kinlaw 1967, 75), and of ʿAmmurapi, a-mu-ra-pí (DULAT 162).

082.evidence: sa with Saporetti, Faucounau, Nahm, Olivier and Valério and the homomorph with Linear A *31 sa (Valério 2016, 655; Davis 2026b, 398); É. Masson read ḫe/ḫi. On RASH Atab 004 it writes the ṯ of Kôṯar in ko-sa-ra-pi, as the Akkadian texts of Ugarit write it with š, ku-šar-a-bi (Kinlaw 1967, 75).

087.evidence: la with Saporetti, Faucounau, Nahm and Valério and the homomorph with Linear A *60 (Valério 2016, 655; Davis 2026b, 398); É. Masson read tˣ. On RASH Atab 004 it writes the l of a-ka-la and a-ka-la-pi, on the Hurrian aġl- of a-ḫa-la-e and a-ga-li-bi (DULAT 29, 25), which Valério sets aside as matches (2016, 363, 371).

091.evidence: mi with Saporetti, Nahm and Valério (Valério 2016, 655). On RASH Atab 004 it writes the m of ʾUmmī- in u-mi-mo-ti (DULAT 68: ủmmt).

092.evidence: sa with Nahm, as Valério reports Nahm's readings of A.11, B.18 and B.19 (2016, 377–378, 389); Faucounau read zi (1977, 235), and Valério weighs zi and leaves the sign without a value (2016, 378–379). Read sa, B.19's 092-011-096 is sa-pe-ri, Ugaritic spr 'scribe', after the name Šapši-maliki; Valério discards the reading (2016, 389). The subscript keeps it apart from 082.

095.evidence: wa with Saporetti, Faucounau, Nahm and Valério (Valério 2016, 655); É. Masson read wa in A.11 (1974, 46). On RASH Atab 004 it gives the -wa-ni of A.11, the ending É. Masson compares with the Luwian ethnic -wanni- (1974, 43).

096.evidence: ri with Nahm and Valério (Valério 2016, 656); É. Masson, Saporetti and Faucounau read ru. On RASH Atab 004 it closes ʾIlī-ṯtamri, i-li-ta-ma-ri (DULAT 65: ỉlṯtmr), as the Akkadian texts of Ugarit spell the second element in a-mis-tam-ri (Kinlaw 1967, 21).

100.evidence: ni with É. Masson, Nahm and Valério (Valério 2016, 654); Faucounau read nu. On RASH Atab 004 it closes ʾIlyāni and Danāni, DINGIR-ia-nu and da-na-nu at Ugarit (DULAT 66, 274), in the genitive Valério reads in every name of the tablet (2016, 395).

102.evidence: a with every proposer (Valério 2016, 656) and the homomorph with Linear A *08 a (Davis 2026b, 398). On RASH Atab 004 it opens ʿAmmurapi, a-mu-ra-pí at Ugarit (DULAT 162), and ʾAġalʾabī (DULAT 25: a-ga-li-bi).

104.evidence: i with every proposer but Sittig, who read e (Valério 2016, 656). On RASH Atab 004 it opens ʾIlī-maliki, ʾIlyāni and ʾIlī-ṯtamri (DULAT 55, 66, 65) and ʾIšbaʿli (DULAT 112).

RASH Atab 004.notes:
A list of men, each named alone, with his father ('PN son of PN') or with his town ('PN, of GN'), as É. Masson read it (1974, 38) after Schaeffer's suggestion of a list of names (O. Masson 1969, 392 n. 22), closing with lines that name a minister and a scribe (B.17–19; É. Masson 1974, 34–35; Valério 2016, 356). Its names are those of Ugarit, Semitic with a Hurrian share, and its bn 'son' and its names in the genitive, ʾIlyāni of Siyannu among them, point to a Semitic language, as Valério concludes (2016, 395). Most identifications are those of Saporetti, Nahm, Faucounau and Valério, credited word by word, read here on one value for each sign.

Of 300 random groups of the same length drawn from the tablet's own signs and set against the syllabic names of the Akkadian texts of Ugarit (Kinlaw 1967), none fits as closely as Kôṯar-ʾabī or ʿAmmurapi, two as closely as ʾIlī-malik and six as ʾIlyānu; the value of 074 was chosen on ʿAmmurapi. Two Enkomi tablets, ENKO Atab 003 and 004, read on the same values, fit the same names in 10% and 3% of their legible groups of three signs or more, against 26% here. One legible group, in A.06, stays unread.

The tablet tells nothing of the languages Cypro-Minoan wrote on Cyprus (É. Masson 1974, 47).
RASH Atab 004.translation: ʾAġlā, son of Mali. ʾAdī, son of ʿAmmusapi. ʾIšbaʿl. ʾAneni, the Maʿqabian. ʾAdattari, son of Tayyānu. ʾIyapati, son of […]. Son of ʾEwenni. ʾAwesapi, son of Kabili. Zidanni. ʾIlyānu, the Siyannian. Danānu, son of ʾIlī-ṯtamar. ʾAnniyānu, son of Sanuwani. ʾUl-ʾAmurru, the Gapanian. Kôṯar-ʾabī. ʾIlī-malik, son of ʾUmmī-môtu. ʾAġalʾabī, son of the king. ʾEwri-tašal, ʾarabimasakuli. ʿAmmurapi; minister of the king […]. Mosani, son of the king. Šapši-malik, scribe; pa.

É. Masson's bi-nu, Semitic bn 'son' (1974, 39), which stands eleven times on the tablet, seven of them between two names, as Ugaritic lists set 'PN bn PN' (DULAT 65: ỉlṯtmr, 'bn PN'), and twice before malki 'of the king' (B.15, B.18). Saporetti and Woudhuizen read pi-ni (Valério 2016, 364; Woudhuizen 2016, 30).

the Hurrian name ati of Nuzi

words.note: Valério's /Aneni/, with Emar a-ni-ni (2016, 375); at Ugarit the name ảnn (DULAT 78).

Nahm's ma-ka-pi-yi, the gentilic mʿqby of the village mʿqb (Valério 2016, 380), which Valério calls ingenious and unambiguous (2016, 380): mʿqby (DULAT 516); Maʿqabu, a town of Ugarit's plain, modern el-ʿAqabé (Astour 1995, 56, 65; Watson 2001, 117). É. Masson read a name and an ethnic in this line (1974, 38).

Valério finds no parallel and sets Addaru aside, since it would make the scribe write one 004 too many (2016, 368). The doubled 004 is the one pair of reduplicated signs in CM 3 (Duhoux, in Steele (ed.) 2013, 40 n. 56).

words.note: As at A.01.

As at A.01.

Valério's e?-wi2??-ni?, Hurrian Even(n)i, Ewen(n)i at Mari (2016, 385–386); the Akkadian texts of Ugarit spell ewen- e-we-en- (Kinlaw 1967, 51). Valério leaves the group unidentified (2016, 386).

words.note: Valério's /ʦidanni/, Luwian Zidanni, Ugarit śdn (2016, 380–381). štn, spelled ša-ta?-na at Ugarit, also fits (DULAT 839).
Faucounau's i-li-ya-nu (1977, 231) and the ilyn of Nahm and Valério (2016, 376): ỉlyn, DINGIR-ia-nu at Ugarit (DULAT 66; Kinlaw 1967, 64).

Nahm's later si-ya-ni-yi and Valério's /ʦijānnīji/ 'from Siyannu' (2016, 380 and n. 1011): the gentilic syny, which follows a name in 'PN syny' (DULAT 763); Siyannu (Astour 1995, 56; Watson 2001, 119).
Faucounau's da-na-nu (1977, 231) and the Danānu of Nahm and Valério (2016, 375): dnn, da-na-nu at Ugarit (DULAT 274; Kinlaw 1967, 47).

ảnnyn, spelled a-na-an-ia-nu and a-na-ni-ya(-a)-nu at Ugarit, perhaps Hurrian (DULAT 79). Both spellings write two syllables with n, a-na-n(i)-, where the group writes one, a-ne-; Valério sets these names under Hurrian anan- 'rejoice' (2016, 376).

Valério's text marks the first sign erased (2016, 549–550), which É. Masson also leaves out (1974, 32). Valério reads 'from Gap(a)nu(?)' and sets aside gpny (2016, 381, 391); gpn is a town of Ugarit, spelled gup-na (Watson 2001, 114).

words.note: Saporetti's Ko-sa-ra-bi, ku-šar-a-bu 'Kōṯaru is my father' (Valério 2016, 370), which Valério calls a clear-cut match (2016, 370): ku-šar-a-bi in the Akkadian texts of Ugarit, borne by a son of Šaiya at RS 16.242:5 (Kinlaw 1967, 75). Every sign takes the value most proposers give it, and of 300 random groups of four signs drawn from the tablet none fits a name of Ugarit as closely.

Saporetti's i-li-mi-li-ki, ilmlk 'My god is king', Nahm's i-li-ma-li-ki and Valério's /ʾIlīmalik/ (2016, 370–371): ỉlmlk (DULAT 55–56), written ili-milku and ilim-mu-lik in the Akkadian texts of Ugarit (Kinlaw 1967, 62, 63). Its ma-li-ki is /malik/, the form of the divine name in ᵈma-lik beside /milku/, where the noun 'king' was /malku/ (McAffee 2019, 238 n. 217), whose genitive the tablet spells ma-ki with the l unwritten (B.15). Valério translates the name 'My god is king' and allows 'My god is Malik' (2016, 371 and n. 948).
As at A.01.

Nahm's ummt and Valério's /ʾUmmīmōtu/, 'My mother is Mōtu' (2016, 371): ủmmt, set as 'bn ủmmt' in the lists of Ugarit (DULAT 68). The mo of 073 writes the ō of Ugaritic /mōtu/ < *mawtu, as Valério argues (2016, 371), McAffee's /môtu/ < /*mawtu/ 'death' (2019, 13), which the alphabet's mt leaves open to confusion with /mutu/ 'man' (McAffee 2019, 14).

špšmlk, spelled ᵈUTU-LUGAL at Ugarit, among others in the colophon of RS 20.32 (DULAT 825), written here with the p in coda unwritten; Valério's earlier /Šapšu-malik/, which Valério sets aside (2016, 389). The second element is /malik/, as at B.14.

Nahm's sa-pe-ri, Ugaritic spr 'scribe' (Valério 2016, 389), which Valério discards (2016, 389); 011 is a sign here, not a divider (Egetmeyer, in Steele (ed.) 2013, 111). B.17–19 close the tablet (É. Masson 1974, 34–35; Valério 2016, 356).
